race:dwarf.title: Dwarves
race:dwarf.summary: Short, broad, loud and patient as stone. Dwarves live inside the Greyteeth, keep every promise and every grudge in the same book, and brew the best ale in the world.

sections.title: Who they are
sections.text: Dwarves say they were woken by the ringing of the mountains as the dragons shaped them in the [[era:dawnfire|Dawnfire]], and that they have been hammering back ever since. They live about three hundred years, grow beards from their first century, and measure a person by what they make and whether they keep their word.

sections.title: Where they live
sections.text: Inside the [[place:greyteeth|Greyteeth]], in holds linked by the [[place:long-road|Long Road]]. The three great holds are [[culture:dwarf.ironhold|Ironhold]] of the smiths, [[culture:dwarf.brewhall|Brewhall]] of the brewers and storytellers, and [[culture:dwarf.runedeep|Runedeep]] of the rune-priests and delvers. Every clan has a hall, and every hall has a door with names carved above it.

sections.title: The clan book
sections.text: Every dwarf clan keeps one great book. It records debts owed, debts paid, grudges held and grudges settled, which dwarves consider the same thing. A name carved above the clan door is an honour. A name chiselled out is the worst thing that can happen to a dwarf, and to their grandchildren.

sections.title: Among the Pact
sections.text: Durga Stonesong of the [[era:first-five|First Five]] was a rune-priest of Runedeep, and carved the seal on the [[hollow:cinder-gate|Cinder Gate]]. Dwarves have trusted the [[faction:pact|Pact]] ever since, partly because it keeps its word and partly because Durga wrote it in the clan book.

quote: Carve it, or it did not happen.

heritage:dwarf.title: Dwarven Heritage
heritage:dwarf.summary: Dwarven heritage is carved: names above the clan door, deeds in the clan book, sagas in the hall. Renown is how much of you the clan will carve, and it grows fastest when your kin witness it.

sections.title: Witnessed deeds
sections.text: A dwarf's deed only counts when another dwarf saw it and will swear to it at the clan book. That is why dwarves fighting together earn Renown so much faster: every swing has a witness, and the witness will tell it twice.

heritage:dwarf.trunk0.title: Stout
heritage:dwarf.trunk0.summary: Dwarves are built like the mountain: wide at the bottom and very hard to move.

heritage:dwarf.trunk1.title: Deep Lungs
heritage:dwarf.trunk1.summary: Generations of tunnel air, forge smoke and long shouting have given dwarves breath that outlasts any fight.

heritage:dwarf.trunk2.title: Sagas
heritage:dwarf.trunk2.summary: The sagas of the hall, sung at every feast. Each deed added brings more Renown.

heritage:dwarf.ironhold0.title: Forged
heritage:dwarf.ironhold0.summary: Ironhold dwarves grow up at the anvil and come out of it as tough as anything they make.

heritage:dwarf.ironhold1.title: Iron Grip
heritage:dwarf.ironhold1.summary: A smith's grip, built by years of hammer and tongs, that does not let go of a weapon or a promise.

heritage:dwarf.ironhold2.title: Ironhold Kinship
heritage:dwarf.ironhold2.summary: The shieldwall of Ironhold. Two Ironhold dwarves side by side are already a wall.

heritage:dwarf.brewhall0.title: Hearty Stew
heritage:dwarf.brewhall0.summary: Brewhall cooking puts meat on any bones. A dwarf raised on it shrugs off what would floor anyone else.

heritage:dwarf.brewhall1.title: Good Company
heritage:dwarf.brewhall1.summary: Brewhall's real gift is its tables, where everyone leaves stronger than they came.

heritage:dwarf.brewhall2.title: Brewhall Kinship
heritage:dwarf.brewhall2.summary: Two Brewhall dwarves in a band means someone is always telling the story of the fight while it is happening.

heritage:dwarf.runedeep0.title: Rune Lore
heritage:dwarf.runedeep0.summary: The rune-priests' knowledge of the stone's speech, which puts power into every strike.

heritage:dwarf.runedeep1.title: Delver
heritage:dwarf.runedeep1.summary: The instincts of the deep delvers, who find ore, treasure and danger by the feel of the rock.

heritage:dwarf.runedeep2.title: Runedeep Kinship
heritage:dwarf.runedeep2.summary: Rune-sworn brotherhoods fight as one rune carved in many hands.

culture:dwarf.ironhold.title: Ironhold
culture:dwarf.ironhold.summary: The greatest of the dwarf holds: a mountain hollowed into forges, where the hammers never stop and the shieldwall has never broken.

sections.title: The hold
sections.text: Ironhold is carved around the great forge-shaft, a column of hot air rising from deep in the [[place:greyteeth|Greyteeth]]. Its halls ring with hammers day and night, and its gates were forged by the greatest smiths in dwarven history, with their names carved above them.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Ironhold dwarves are smiths, shieldwrights, miners and soldiers. They value craft, order and the wall: the line of shields that holds the deep tunnels. An Ironhold beardling serves in the shieldwall before their beard comes in, and never forgets it.

sections.title: The clans
sections.text: Ironhold is ruled by its oldest clans, whose halls are full of cousins and whose clan books are the thickest. Being heir to one is an honour that comes with a great many relatives' opinions.

facts: A fist on the chest, and your clan name
quote: The wall matters more than the dwarf.

culture:dwarf.brewhall.title: Brewhall
culture:dwarf.brewhall.summary: The warm, loud, crowded hold where the dwarves brew, cook and sing. Every dwarf wedding wants Brewhall ale, and every saga is sung best in its halls.

sections.title: The hold
sections.text: Brewhall is built around a hot spring warmed by the [[world:underflame|Underflame]], which the dwarves use for everything from brewing to bathing. Its cellars hold barrels older than most human kingdoms. Its great hall seats two thousand and is full most nights.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Brewhall dwarves are brewers, cooks, innkeepers and skalds. They believe a good meal and a good story mend more than any healer, and they may be right. They are the friendliest of the dwarves, which is not saying much, and the best at getting other peoples drunk.

sections.title: The contest
sections.text: The Brewhall drinking contest is held every midwinter. Winning it three years running puts your name in the clan book, which tells you how seriously dwarves take ale.

facts: Ale, stew, sagas, the drinking contest
A full tankard, pushed across the table
quote: Patience is just thirst with discipline.

culture:dwarf.runedeep.title: Runedeep
culture:dwarf.runedeep.summary: The deepest of the holds, where the rune-priests listen to the stone, carve the wards that hold the fire down, and delvers map tunnels no dwarf has walked in a thousand years.

sections.title: The hold
sections.text: Runedeep is dug down rather than in, a great spiral stair into the roots of the [[place:greyteeth|Greyteeth]]. Its lowest gates are carved with the warding runes that keep the [[world:underflame|Underflame]] and whatever lives in it below. Lately those runes are warm.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Runedeep dwarves are rune-priests of the [[faith:runes|Rune Faith]], carvers and deep delvers. They are quieter than other dwarves, because they spend their lives listening. A rune-sworn dwarf belongs to a brotherhood of priests bound by an oath-rune carved on all of them.

sections.title: Durga's hold
sections.text: Durga Stonesong of the [[era:first-five|First Five]] was a priest of Runedeep. Her runes sealed the [[hollow:cinder-gate|Cinder Gate]], and her name is the first carved above Runedeep's door.

facts: A palm laid flat on the nearest stone
quote: The stone always speaks. Most people are just too loud to hear it.

backstory:dwarf.smith.title: Forge Apprentice
backstory:dwarf.smith.summary: Grew up at the anvils of Ironhold, with burn scars to prove it and opinions about every blade they see.

sections.title: The forges
sections.text: Ironhold apprentices start at six, pumping bellows. By twelve they are allowed to hold the tongs, and by twenty, if they are good, the hammer.

backstory:dwarf.shieldbearer.title: Shield-bearer
backstory:dwarf.shieldbearer.summary: Held the line in the deep tunnels with Ironhold's shieldwall before their beard came in.

sections.title: The wall
sections.text: The deep tunnels of [[culture:dwarf.ironhold|Ironhold]] are held by a wall of shields against [[beast:goblins|goblins]] and worse. Beardlings serve in its back rank, and learn to stand still while terrible things happen in front of them.

backstory:dwarf.clanheir.title: Clan Heir
backstory:dwarf.clanheir.summary: Heir of an old Ironhold clan, with a hall full of cousins and a clan book full of expectations.

sections.title: Heirs
sections.text: The old clans of [[culture:dwarf.ironhold|Ironhold]] pass their halls to the eldest child who has proved worthy. Proving it usually means a deed worth carving, and the [[faction:pact|Pact]] is full of them.

backstory:dwarf.cook.title: Hall Cook
backstory:dwarf.cook.summary: Fed a hundred miners a day in the halls of Brewhall and never let a pot burn.

sections.title: The kitchens
sections.text: Brewhall's kitchens run every hour of the day, because miners work every hour of the day. A cook there learns speed, temper and how to stop a fight with a ladle.

backstory:dwarf.brewer.title: Brewer's Child
backstory:dwarf.brewer.summary: Knows every barrel in Brewhall by its smell, and most of them by their first name.

sections.title: The cellars
sections.text: The cellars of [[culture:dwarf.brewhall|Brewhall]] hold barrels older than kingdoms. Brewing families keep their recipes in no book at all, only in their noses.

backstory:dwarf.skald.title: Tavern Skald
backstory:dwarf.skald.summary: Told the old sagas in the halls of Brewhall until the whole hall sang along.

sections.title: Skalds
sections.text: A skald of [[culture:dwarf.brewhall|Brewhall]] knows the sagas of every clan, and which verses not to sing when certain clans are in the room.

backstory:dwarf.runecarver.title: Runecarver
backstory:dwarf.runecarver.summary: Carved warding runes into the deepest gates of Runedeep, where the stone is warm and the dark is listening.

sections.title: The deep gates
sections.text: The warding runes on Runedeep's lowest gates must be recut every few years, because the heat beneath slowly wears them. Since the [[era:waking|Waking]], every few months.

backstory:dwarf.delver.title: Deep Delver
backstory:dwarf.delver.summary: Mapped tunnels under Runedeep that no dwarf had walked in a thousand years.

sections.title: Delvers
sections.text: Delvers go below the [[place:long-road|Long Road]] into the cracks the Sundering opened. They map, they mark, and they come back with stories they only tell to other delvers.

backstory:dwarf.runekin.title: Rune-sworn
backstory:dwarf.runekin.summary: Bound by an oath-rune to a brotherhood of Runedeep priests, who share each other's strength.

sections.title: Oath-runes
sections.text: A rune-sworn dwarf carries the brotherhood's rune carved on a stone and pressed into their skin. The priests say they can feel each other across any distance.

answer:dwarf.grandparents.0.summary: The forge-masters who made the great gates of the holds are carved above Ironhold's own door. Their gates have never been broken.

answer:dwarf.grandparents.1.summary: A chiselled-out name is the deepest shame in dwarven life. The clan remembers it for exactly as long as it takes to wash it clean.

answer:dwarf.grandparents.2.summary: The Long Road was found, not dug, at first: an ancient crack the Sundering opened, which dwarves followed and then widened.

answer:dwarf.grandparents.3.summary: Brewhall recipes pass down only by nose. An ale still served at weddings a century later is the highest honour a brewer can win.

answer:dwarf.parents.0.summary: Miners are the backbone of every hold, and the first to know when the stone grows warm and a Hollow is coming.

answer:dwarf.parents.1.summary: Shieldwrights of Ironhold test every shield with a hammer before it leaves the shop. The shieldwall depends on it.

answer:dwarf.parents.2.summary: Gem-cutters keep the treasuries of the holds, and are trusted with the clan's wealth because they are trusted with its count.

answer:dwarf.parents.3.summary: Every clan's book of grudges is also its book of debts. Its keepers are feared, respected and invited to everything.

answer:dwarf.siblings.0.summary: Dwarven clan halls house whole families together, and a dozen cousins is a small hall.

answer:dwarf.siblings.1.summary: The hold guard stands at the gates and in the tunnels. A sibling in it is a hero to every beardling.

answer:dwarf.siblings.2.summary: Great-uncles are the keepers of every story nobody else wants to tell, and most of the useful ones.

answer:dwarf.siblings.3.summary: Dwarves sometimes foster human children from the Highmarch, after raids or bad winters. The doorways are always a problem.

answer:dwarf.birth.0.summary: Cave-ins are remembered by gallery number. Every dwarf born during one is said to carry the luck of those who were dug out.

answer:dwarf.birth.1.summary: True mithril is rare and found only near the old cracks of the Sundering, where the Underflame has run for a thousand years.

answer:dwarf.birth.2.summary: The great forges of the holds burn on the Underflame's heat. Relighting one after a century is a festival for the whole mountain.

answer:dwarf.birth.3.summary: Earthquakes under the Greyteeth are more common since the Waking. The rune-priests listen to every one.

answer:dwarf.friend.0.summary: Mine ponies haul the carts of the Long Road, and are as stubborn as their dwarves.

answer:dwarf.friend.1.summary: Gnome tinkers trade with the dwarf holds and are tolerated for their clever work and despite their explosions.

answer:dwarf.friend.2.summary: Shield-twins are dwarves born on the same day and sworn to the same line in the shieldwall, for life.

answer:dwarf.friend.3.summary: Cave spiders are common in the deep tunnels. Most are harmless. Most.

answer:dwarf.play.0.summary: Dwarven children are given a hammer as soon as they can lift one, and nothing in the hold is safe after that.

answer:dwarf.play.1.summary: Abandoned tunnels lead off the Long Road everywhere. Children explore them; parents pretend not to know.

answer:dwarf.play.2.summary: Every dwarven hall has a fire and a saga every night. Children who listen well become skalds.

answer:dwarf.play.3.summary: Dwarves can tell real gold by its ring. Children learn by counting the family hoard until they are told to stop.

answer:dwarf.teen.0.summary: Ironhold forge apprentices lose their eyebrows at least once. It is considered a coming of age.

answer:dwarf.teen.1.summary: Brewhall's brewery delivers to every hall in the hold. Its runners are paid in coin and, unofficially, in samples.

answer:dwarf.teen.2.summary: Tunnel patrols walk the darker stretches of the Long Road, where goblins nest and worse things listen.

answer:dwarf.teen.3.summary: Rune-priests of Runedeep take students young, so the stone's voice is learned before the ears grow stubborn.

answer:dwarf.firstfight.0.summary: Goblins raid the deep halls for metal and food. Every dwarf's first fight seems to be against them.

answer:dwarf.firstfight.1.summary: Tavern brawls in Brewhall are a cherished tradition, with rules about what may not be thrown.

answer:dwarf.firstfight.2.summary: Trolls try the hold gates every winter. They are held with shields while others strike, the way every dwarf learns to fight.

answer:dwarf.firstfight.3.summary: Grudge duels settle what is written in the clan book. An unresolved one is written there too, and waits.

answer:dwarf.mentor.0.summary: Ironhold shieldmasters teach that the wall matters more than the dwarf, and that the Pact's first rule is a dwarven one.

answer:dwarf.mentor.1.summary: Rune-priests say the stone has moods: patient, angry, frightened. Lately, under the deep gates, frightened.

answer:dwarf.mentor.2.summary: Brewhall brewers are the philosophers of the holds, and their sayings are carved in the hall beams.

answer:dwarf.mentor.3.summary: Dwarven merchants trade with the surface at Lanternford and Freeport, and are the reason the holds know anything about the sky.

answer:dwarf.leaving.0.summary: Grudges in the clan book do not expire. A dwarf can settle one written two hundred years before they were born.

answer:dwarf.leaving.1.summary: New ore turns up near new Hollows, where the Underflame has melted the rock into something strange.

answer:dwarf.leaving.2.summary: An oathbreaker's shame is washed off with a deed great enough to carve. The Pact's Hollows have restored many clan names.

answer:dwarf.leaving.3.summary: Dwarves who see the sky for the first time often lie down flat. It is too big, and they are sure it will fall.

answer:dwarf.deed.0.summary: A masterwork carried by a king is the proudest thing an Ironhold smith can make.

answer:dwarf.deed.1.summary: Digging out survivors after a collapse is the deed dwarves honour most, above any battle.

answer:dwarf.deed.2.summary: Three Brewhall drinking contests in a row puts a name in the clan book. Dwarves do not consider this a joke.

answer:dwarf.deed.3.summary: Clan relics lost in floods and cave-ins wait in the deep halls. Recovering one is a deed for the sagas.

answer:dwarf.loss.0.summary: A dwarf whose shield-twin falls keeps their place in the wall empty for a year.

answer:dwarf.loss.1.summary: Several small holds have been lost since the Waking, to things that came up through the floor.

answer:dwarf.loss.2.summary: Dwarves do not trust elven merchants, and every clan book has a page that explains why.

answer:dwarf.loss.3.summary: Brewhall holds that there is no loss so great a good ale cannot shrink it a little.

answer:dwarf.fear.0.summary: Most dwarves who leave the holds never get used to the open sky. There is nothing holding it up.

answer:dwarf.fear.1.summary: To be chiselled from above the clan door is to be erased from dwarven memory.

answer:dwarf.fear.2.summary: Delvers say something sleeps under the deepest halls. The rune-priests say not to wake it.

answer:dwarf.fear.3.summary: An empty tankard and an empty purse on the same day is the oldest dwarven curse.

answer:dwarf.keepsake.0.summary: Forge hammers are passed down until there is more wear than hammer, and then passed down anyway.

answer:dwarf.keepsake.1.summary: Rune-stones carved in Runedeep warm when the Underflame is near, which is why every delver carries one.

answer:dwarf.keepsake.2.summary: Beard beads mark a dwarf's clan and deeds. One from a clan's first hoard is a treasure beyond its gold.

answer:dwarf.keepsake.3.summary: Brewhall stout is said to cure fear, cold and bad news. Dwarves carry it for all three.

answer:dwarf.drive.0.summary: Clan honour is measured in what is carved above the door and what is struck from the book.

answer:dwarf.drive.1.summary: Dwarves love gold openly and count it loudly. Hollows are full of it, which helps the Pact recruit dwarves.

answer:dwarf.drive.2.summary: Every dwarven smith dreams of one masterwork that will outlast the mountain.

answer:dwarf.drive.3.summary: Dwarves who lost their holds since the Waking wander the surface, and some are trying to build new ones.
